name: [BUAMS] KUL 14 INTRODUCTION TO AI
text:
FKIK UIN Maulana Malik Ibrahim
Malang
Artificial 
Intelligence
in Healthcare settings
dr. Abdul Malik Setiawan, 
M.Infect.Dis.
Presenter:
Understand the principles of AI in healthcare
Identify the challenges of implementing AI in medicine
Evaluate the ethical aspects and responsibilities of 
using AI in medicine
Describe the classification of AI applications in medicine
Learning outcome
• Patient → AI rapidly analyzes X-ray
• AI in radiology, oncology, hospital 
management
• Future doctors must understand AI
• Principles – classification – opportunities – 
considerations – challenges – ethics
• Doctors = tech-savvy & ethically responsible
Why use AI?
• Artificial Intelligence (AI): Broad field of creating 
machines with human-like intelligence.
• Machine Learning (ML): AI subset; systems learn 
from data to improve performance.
• Deep Learning (DL): ML using multi-layered 
neural networks for complex data (e.g., medical 
images).
• Natural Language Processing (NLP): AI branch 
for understanding and generating human 
language.
• Large Language Models (LLMs): Advanced NLP 
systems trained on massive text data, producing 
human-like responses.
AI by definition
How does AI work in medicine
Input → Algorithm → Output
Machine Learning → predicts 
clinical patterns
Deep Learning → medical 
image analysis
Examples:
AI reading chest X-ray
Predicting diabetes risk from MR
Types and Applications of AI 
in Medicine
Data-driven AI → prognosis, patient management
Device-based AI → wearables, telemedicine, patient 
monitoring
Therapeutic AI → radiotherapy planning, precision 
medicine
Competencies for the use of AI 
by healthcare professionals
Workflow analysis for AI-
based tools
Basic knowledge of AI
Social & ethical 
implications of AI
Evidence-based evaluation of AI 
tools
AI-enhanced clinical encounters
continuous learning & practice on 
AI-based tools
Ethics and Regulation
Ethics in AI
Necessary Regulation
• Using AI for the common good
• Protection of human rights
• Transparency of AI systems
• Accountability for AI impacts
The Importance of the
Young Generation
Digital Natives
Ethical Responsibility
Fresh Perspectives
Driving Demand
Future Innovators
Conclusion of 
Presentation
Great opportunities await, but must be 
accompanied by responsibility
Depending on how we use it
AI is a tool, not a threat!
Thank You!
FKIK UIN Maulana Malik Ibrahim
Malang
Use of AI Tools to 
Enhance Medical 
Student Learning
dr. Abdul Malik Setiawan, M.Infect.Dis
Presenter:
Describe various AI-powered tools in medical 
education.
Analyze the benefits and opportunities of using AI
Evaluate the limitations and challenges of AI tools in medical 
education.
Identify the applications of AI in different areas of medical learning
Learning outcome
• Why medical education needs innovation
• Growth of AI in higher education
• Medical students face massive content & 
skill demands
• AI as a potential learning assistant
• Easy and cheap in comparison with 
multiple text books
Why use AI?
How does AI work in medicine
Content generation tools → 
create study notes, summaries, 
flashcards
Adaptive learning platforms → 
personalized quizzes & learning
Chatbots & virtual tutors → 
24/7 interactive Q&A support
Simulation & virtual patient AI → 
practice clinical reasoning & decision-making
AI Tools for Biomedicine
3D anatomy visualization with AI (e.g., Complete Anatomy, 
BioDigital Human)
AI quiz generators for recall & spaced repetition
Example: Questgen, Quillionz, PrepAI, Quizgecko
Generative AI to create diagrams & practice questions
Example: ChatGPT, Bing Copilot
AI Tools for Clinical 
Reasoning
Virtual patient simulators with 
AI-driven scenarios
Decision-support practice platforms (AI 
creates differential diagnosis lists)
Conversational AI for case-
based discussion
AI support for ICD-10 diagnosis list
AI Tools for Assessment & 
Feedback
Automated scoring of short-answer/essay questions
Example: Gradescope, ChatGPT
AI-driven OSCE evaluation (checklists, communication 
analysis). Example: Geeky Medics, Neural consult, ChatGPT
Plagiarism and originality detection
Example: Turnitin
Limitations & Challenges
Risk of misinformation or 
hallucinations (AI-generated 
errors)
Over-reliance → reduced critical 
thinking
Cost & accessibility of advanced 
platforms
Integration with curriculum and 
accreditation standards
Ethical Considerations
Fairness and bias in AI-generated content
Academic integrity: balancing AI assistance vs. cheating
Equity in access to AI tools
Transparency of algorithms & explainability
Benefits: personalization, feedback, engagement, accessibility
Medical students should learn to be critical, ethical, and creative 
users of AI in their education
AI tools can enhance medical student learning across domains 
(knowledge, skills, reasoning, assessment)
Challenges: accuracy, ethics, reliance, integration
Summary & Take Home Message
Thank You!
